question: Is the composition 0.000 a no-viable-code generation failure or a wrong-program (semantic) failure, and does it survive length-matched and surface-matched controls?

controls.e_per_composite_decomposition: every condition x op reports syntax / valid / solve-defined / executable / pass@1 + parse|allowlist|zero_pass|partial|all_pass

design: matched controls around the exposure experiment: one model trained on primitives + exposed composites (identical to run_composition_exposure), seven conditions forming a structure x surface 2x2 at primitive-matched program length, with paired instances (ref code + hidden tests held fixed, only the prompt changes)
seeding_note: exact run_composition_exposure.py recipe: torch.manual_seed(seed) only; the global-random batch sampler is left unseeded as in the original exposure runs (completed checkpoints archived, so all reported numbers are exact; eval is reseeded per condition and fully deterministic). A prior attempt that also seeded global random is archived as *_bothseeded.* — its seed-1 batch stream diverged late in training (full-train loss 0.1645 vs 0.033 typical), which would have confounded the matched controls with a weak base model.

tokenizer.corpus: train+exposed then heldout (exact exposure order); control texts rely on the complete byte alphabet

decode.early_stop: 16 consecutive NUL tokens (lossless for NUL-truncated extraction)

length_matching.note: token counts under the run tokenizer; new composites asserted inside the mastered-primitive range (control c)

primitive_unseen_surface.role: control (a): SEEN program structure, UNSEEN wording — reference code and hidden tests byte-identical to primitive_native

exposed_native.role: anchor: composites seen in training (pipeline upper bound)

heldout_native.role: baseline: the book's failing condition (unseen composite, native unseen family prompt)

heldout_seen_surface.role: control (b): UNSEEN composite structure under a VERBATIM training surface frame — ref code + tests identical to heldout_native

new_composite_unseen_surface.role: control (c): NEW length-matched composite, novel wording — 2x2 cell unseen structure x unseen surface

new_composite_seen_surface.role: control (c)+(b): NEW length-matched composite under a VERBATIM training frame — 2x2 cell unseen structure x seen surface

decomposition: per-condition failure decomposition (favorable256 decode; no-viable-code | incomplete | wrong-semantics | pass): primitive_native: 0/300 no-viable-code (syntax 1.000), 0/300 incomplete (parses but defines no solve), 0/300 wrong-semantics (complete program, runs, fails tests), 300/300 pass (pass@1 1.000, complete-program rate 1.000); primitive_unseen_surface: 298/300 no-viable-code (syntax 0.017), 0/300 incomplete (parses but defines no solve), 2/300 wrong-semantics (complete program, runs, fails tests), 0/300 pass (pass@1 0.000, complete-program rate 0.007); exposed_native: 39/120 no-viable-code (syntax 0.675), 0/120 incomplete (parses but defines no solve), 1/120 wrong-semantics (complete program, runs, fails tests), 80/120 pass (pass@1 0.667, complete-program rate 0.675); heldout_native: 120/120 no-viable-code (syntax 0.000), 0/120 incomplete (parses but defines no solve), 0/120 wrong-semantics (complete program, runs, fails tests), 0/120 pass (pass@1 0.000, complete-program rate 0.000); heldout_seen_surface: 120/120 no-viable-code (syntax 0.000), 0/120 incomplete (parses but defines no solve), 0/120 wrong-semantics (complete program, runs, fails tests), 0/120 pass (pass@1 0.000, complete-program rate 0.000); new_composite_unseen_surface: 44/80 no-viable-code (syntax 0.463), 36/80 incomplete (parses but defines no solve), 0/80 wrong-semantics (complete program, runs, fails tests), 0/80 pass (pass@1 0.000, complete-program rate 0.000); new_composite_seen_surface: 80/80 no-viable-code (syntax 0.000), 0/80 incomplete (parses but defines no solve), 0/80 wrong-semantics (complete program, runs, fails tests), 0/80 pass (pass@1 0.000, complete-program rate 0.000)
conclusion: **Held-out composites (baseline) are a pure no-viable-code (0/120 define a complete solve program; syntax 0.000) failure**: 120/120 no-viable-code + 0/120 incomplete, 0/120 wrong-semantics under the most favorable decode (favorable256; book_prefix80 syntax 0.000), so the 0.000 is not 'parses but computes the wrong composition' — semantics are never reached. The same pipeline scores complete-program rate 1.000/pass@1 1.000 on primitives and complete-program rate 0.675/pass@1 0.667 on exposed composites, so the pipeline itself is sound. **Wording axis (control a)**: rewording MASTERED primitive programs with never-seen template families yields syntax 0.017, complete-program rate 0.007 and pass@1 0.000 (298/300 no-viable-code + 0/300 incomplete) vs syntax 1.000/complete 1.000/pass@1 1.000 for the native wording — novel wording alone ALSO collapses generation, so surface-OD is a real contributor and must be controlled for — see control (b). **Surface-matched control (b)**: the identical held-out composite programs under verbatim training frames score syntax 0.000, complete-program rate 0.000, executable 0.000, pass@1 0.000 (120/120 no-viable-code + 0/120 incomplete, 0/120 wrong-semantics) vs the native-prompt baseline syntax 0.000/pass@1 0.000 — verbatim frames move the complete-program rate only 0.000 -> 0.000 and pass@1 stays 0.000: no rescue, so the wording FRAME is not the confound. **Length-matched control (c)**: the NEW composites (reference token length asserted inside the mastered-primitive range) score unseen-surface complete-program rate 0.000/pass@1 0.000 (44/80 no-viable-code + 36/80 incomplete, 0/80 wrong-semantics; per op: abs_mul: syntax 0.925/complete 0.000/pass 0.000; first_plus_len: syntax 0.000/complete 0.000/pass 0.000) and seen-frame complete-program rate 0.000/pass@1 0.000 (80/80 no-viable-code + 0/80 incomplete) — length is NOT the confound: at primitive-matched length the unseen composite still fails to produce a complete program. **Verdict**: the composition 0.000 IS a no-viable-code generation failure (120/120 without a complete program, 0/120 wrong-semantics — semantics are never reached), and it SURVIVES both matched controls: verbatim training frames (b) leave 120/120 without a complete program (complete-program rate 0.000) and pass@1 0.000, and at primitive-matched program length the new composites are 80/80 + 80/80 without a complete program under BOTH wordings (c), pass@1 0.000/0.000 — so neither wording frame nor program length explains the 0.000. IMPORTANT qualification from control (a): rewording MASTERED primitive programs with never-seen families ALSO collapses generation (298/300 without a complete program, complete-program rate 0.007 vs 1.000 native), so no-viable-code is this model's generic response to out-of-distribution prompts, and unseen composite structure is one such trigger — sufficient even when the sentence frame is verbatim from training (prompt length is ruled out: the seen-surface exposed control runs at comparable prompt length with complete-program rate 0.675). The book's structural-generalization conclusion therefore survives the matched controls as a GENERATION failure on unseen compositions (never a wrong-program/semantic failure: composite wrong-semantics counts are held-out 0, seen-surface 0, length-matched 0), but its mechanism is prompt-OD generation collapse, not failed composition attempts: the honest claim is that the model cannot generate code for unseen compositions (nor for seen programs under unseen wording), not that it composes incorrectly.
